study_identification_part.si4_title: Atypical Brain Asymmetry in Autism: A Candidate for Clinically Meaningful Stratification

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Model individual deviations in gray matter hemispheric laterality across age using normative modeling to characterize heterogeneous asymmetry patterns in autism and test their associations with clinical features (e.g., language delay).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Compared % extreme deviations across diagnosis/sex via GLM (age covariate); ROI-based characterization in language/motor/visuospatial networks (FDR-corrected); relative importance analyses in ASD relating deviations to language delay, ADOS CSS, ADHD, handedness, sex.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: ASD shows individualized patterns of both extreme right- and leftward laterality deviations. Language delay relates to greater rightward deviations; core ASD severity relates more to leftward deviations. Results are robust and replicate in ABIDE.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Individuals with autism exhibited significantly more extreme rightward and leftward deviations than NTs. Spatial overlaps highlighted language, motor, and visuospatial regions. Language delay explained most variance in extreme rightward deviations, while core ASD symptom severity (ADOS CSS) explained most variance in extreme leftward deviations. Group-mean PALM analyses were nonsignificant, underscoring the value of individual-level normative modeling. Findings were robust to FDR thresholding and similar when addressing site with ComBat; replication in ABIDE confirmed implicated regions.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Atypical laterality patterns may serve as a neurophenotype for clinically meaningful stratification in autism; the normative approach supports precision stratification beyond case–control contrasts.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Subsample sizes shrink when stratifying by diagnosis, sex, language delay, and site; residual site effects may remain despite modeling site and using ComBat; cross-sectional design limits developmental inference; approach optimized for detecting extremes may be less sensitive to globally reduced lateralization.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: ABIDE replication used harmonized preprocessing (no study-specific DARTEL template; registered to LEAP template). Acquisition was 3T across 5 sites with semi-automated QC; Rome site excluded post-QC due to low N. Site handled as covariate; ComBat explored for robustness.
